name: Romanian Football Championship
content:
The first Romanian football championship was established in 1909 and was organized in a very different way compared to modern league competitions. Instead of a national season-long format, the early championships involved a small number of teams competing in a cup-style structure. Clubs from cities such as Bucharest and Ploiești played an important role during the beginnings of organized football in Romania.

As football became more popular, the competition gradually expanded and regional tournaments started appearing throughout the country. Teams first competed at a local level, and successful clubs advanced to national stages to determine the overall champion. This system allowed football to spread beyond a few major cities and helped create stronger competition across different regions.

The cup-style era continued for more than two decades and laid the foundation for Romanian football development. Although the structure lacked the consistency of a modern league, it helped establish clubs, rivalries, and organizational systems. These early championships played a crucial role in preparing Romanian football for a more professional national structure.

name: Liga I
content:
Romanian football entered a new era in 1932 with the creation of Divizia A, introducing a national league system for the first time. The previous knockout and regional qualification formats were replaced with a season-long competition in which clubs regularly competed against each other. This change marked the beginning of modern top-level football in Romania.

Over the following decades, Divizia A became the country's most important football competition and evolved through various structural changes. The league expanded and adapted over time while surviving major historical events, including political changes and periods of national transformation. It became the stage for many of Romania’s most successful and influential football clubs.

In 2006, the competition was renamed Liga I after trademark-related issues involving the original Divizia A name. Despite the change in branding, the league remained Romania’s highest football division and continued its long tradition. Today Liga I remains the center of professional football in Romania and continues to shape the country's football culture and history.

name: Cupa României
content:
Cupa României is the main national football cup competition in Romania and has been held since 1933. Organized by the Romanian Football Federation, the tournament is open to clubs from different levels of the Romanian football league system, giving smaller teams the opportunity to compete against the country’s biggest clubs. The competition is considered one of the most prestigious football tournaments in Romania and has a long tradition in Romanian sports culture.

The tournament is played in a knockout format, with teams entering at different stages depending on their league level. Over the years, the structure of the competition has changed several times, including the introduction of group stages and revised qualification systems. Winning the cup not only brings a major domestic trophy but also usually grants qualification for European competitions, increasing the importance of the tournament for clubs across the country.

Cupa României has been dominated historically by famous Romanian clubs such as Steaua București, Dinamo București, Rapid București, and CFR Cluj. Many memorable finals and rivalries have helped shape Romanian football history, while smaller clubs have occasionally produced surprising cup runs and upset victories. The final is traditionally one of the biggest sporting events in Romania and attracts strong national attention every season.
